title: Atlas project state (.atlas/project.json)
description: Per-repository Atlas configuration. Written by a human via the adoption skill or the CLI. Agents cannot write this file — see AUTHORITY_MODEL.md.

remote.description: Canonical remote URL. Project identity is this, never a filesystem path.

runtime.description: The pin MUST come from the project (engines/.nvmrc/tool manifest), never from whatever process happens to be running.

node.description: Semver range or exact version, e.g. '20.x'.

validation.description: The validation ladder, in order. Each rung is a package script or command. A skipped rung is NEVER a pass.

invariants.description: The invariant registry. An invariant with no enforcement test is aspirational, not enforced.

design.description: Configures the design-director review. Human-written like the rest of this file — agents cannot write it. A repo with no UI omits this or sets enabled:false; a scoped-out run is a logged skip, NEVER a recorded pass.

harness.description: Command that brings the UI up headless in CI, e.g. 'npm run build && npm run preview -- --port 4173'.

readyUrl.description: URL polled until it returns 200 before capture, e.g. 'http://localhost:4173'.

screens.description: The screens the director reviews. The human declares what matters; a changed-but-undeclared surface is a finding, not a silent pass.

path.description: Route appended to readyUrl, e.g. '/' or '/story/demo'.

paths.description: Globs that make a PR user-facing. A PR touching these makes the design check required; a PR touching none is a logged skip.

functionSignal.description: The repo's own end-to-end command, e.g. 'npm run test:e2e'. Its real exit code is the works-as-intended signal; a failure is a NO-GO on its own.

captureCommand.description: Optional. A single-line repo command that renders the declared screens and writes one PNG per screen×viewport to artifacts/design/ — typically a Playwright screenshot spec run under the repo's OWN playwright.config, which already boots the server, authenticates, provisions a DB, and resolves the browser. Set this for apps behind auth or needing a database (the built-in harness+readyUrl+goto path would only screenshot the auth wall). When set, harness/readyUrl are ignored and the command's exit code is the harness signal. When omitted, the built-in generic capture is used.

browsers.description: Playwright browsers to install/capture with, sourced from playwright.config projects[].use.browserName. Default chromium.

gates.description: Where human authority actually lives. These are external systems, deliberately.

acceptanceGate.description: Who records acceptance and how, e.g. 'human:cli:atlas-accept'
